titulo: Your storyboard: a 30 s scene broken into shots and checked
lead: Time to put it all together: the director's card, the character sheet, the look and the shot list become a 30-second storyboard, checked by the page. It's the package you take to any generator, and it's where course 1 starts.
objetivo: combine the card, character sheet, look, and shot list into a 30 s storyboard checked against the page, ready to become a prompt.

aprende.t: See the course map and what each step delivers
Build the 30 s storyboard with a header and shots
Check the whole package before generating
Generate your study plan with dates

hero_alt: Pre-production wall with eight pencil storyboard frames pinned in two rows, on a table with pencils and yellow gaffer tape.

secoes.sub: Four steps that become your storyboard. Click an exercise to see its "done when".

degraus.passo: What the audience should feel, the anchor, and why you chose the angle, movement, duration and light. It is the header of the storyboard.
Size, angle and one movement per shot, each choice made for its effect on the audience.
Fixed light and palette, layered composition and a locked character. This is what holds continuity together.
The scene cut into numbered shots, with camera, sound and timing. This lesson's storyboard comes from here.

resultado.titulo: At the end of the course
resultado.texto: A folder with the card, character sheet, look and a 30 s storyboard, ready for any generator.

rolagem_fim.texto: Four steps, each with its file checked by the page. This lesson's storyboard brings them all together.

secoes.legenda: Suggested order: each step uses what the previous one decided.

secoes.sub: A header with the fixed decisions and one line per shot.

texto: Scene, anchor and emotion come from the card. The character sheet and the look go in one line each, summarized: this is the snippet that repeats in every prompt.
If a line in the header changes midway, every shot changes with it.
The shot list from lesson 7 grows to 30 seconds: 6 to 10 shots, each with size, angle, one movement, duration, action and sound.
Vary it: at least 3 sizes, 2 angles and 3 movements. Open by setting the scene, move in closer at the turn, and close on an image that works as a still.
The page checks the whole package in seconds. Fixing a line of text costs nothing; redoing a generation costs time and credits.
Only take to the generator the storyboard that has already answered OK.
In course 1, each line of this storyboard becomes a prompt, with the character sheet as a reference and the look as a fixed block.
Keep the project folder: it is the one you open in the first lesson there.

secoes.sub: The complete storyboard: header and shots.

secoes.exemplo:
Scene: The first batch (30 s)
Anchor: Dona Lia; everything serves her quiet pride
Emotion: the pride and warmth of being the first one there
Sheet: Dona Lia, 58 years old; hair in a bun with a headscarf, glasses, navy-blue apron, wooden peel
Look: side light from the oven, soft and warm inside; cold, dark street; low-key; steam in the beam
# n | size | angle | movement | duration | what happens | sound
1 | wide shot | high angle | static camera | 4 s | Dark street; only the bakery window is lit. | sound: wind, a dog far away
2 | wide shot | eye level | lateral tracking shot | 4 s | Dona Lia turns on the lights and ties her apron. | sound: light switch, low radio
3 | medium shot | eye level | static camera | 4 s | She kneads the dough on the counter. | sound: dough slapping on the table

txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

secoes.sub: Five questions about the whole course.

perguntas.p: What goes in the storyboard header?
opcoes: Scene, anchor, emotion, sheet and look.
The list of generators and the price of each one.
The final prompts in English for each shot.
The durations of all the shots, added up.
perguntas.explica: The header holds what applies to every shot and repeats in every prompt. The generator and the final prompt are from course 1; the duration stays on each line.

perguntas.p: Why check the storyboard before generating any video?
opcoes: Because the generator refuses text that hasn't been checked.
Because the law requires an approved storyboard.
Because fixing text costs nothing; generating costs money.
Because the check improves the final resolution.
perguntas.explica: The paper rehearsal is free. A direction mistake found after generation costs time and credits to redo.

perguntas.p: A shot in your storyboard says "orbit and zoom." What does the page answer?
opcoes: OK, because orbit and zoom go well together.
It asks you to pick just one movement for the shot.
OK, as long as the shot lasts more than 4 s.
It asks you to swap the zoom for a handheld camera.
perguntas.explica: One movement per shot (lesson 3). The page points out the shot and asks you to keep just one; if the scene needs both, it needs two shots.

perguntas.p: Which of these keeps the same character in every shot?
opcoes: Always using the same camera movement.
Generating all the shots on the same day.
Asking for high resolution in every prompt.
Repeating the lock from the character sheet in every prompt.
perguntas.explica: The character sheet with the "Never changes" line, repeated in every prompt and backed by the reference images, is what holds the face, clothes and prop steady (lesson 6).

perguntas.p: Which shot usually closes a short scene well?
opcoes: A whip pan to the next scene.
An image that works on its own as a still.
Any shot, because the ending matters little.
A quick zoom and a hard cut in the middle.
perguntas.explica: The last frame is what the audience takes away. Paused on the last second, it has to work as an image: the pull-back that gives the place back, the transformed face.

itens.texto: The generator executes; shot, movement, light, composition and sound are your choices, with a reason behind each.
Card, character sheet, look and storyboard in a folder of your own, checked by the page.
In course 1, each storyboard line becomes a prompt in the generator you choose.
